notes.title: Build 1.4.4 - Bugs Getting Fixed
notes.content:
A patch for the population cap bug has been pushed to Steam. The game should update automatically - you can check the version in the lower left of the start scene look for version 1.4.1 or greater. If the game does not update you may need to restart the Steam client.

The current patch only includes this fix as it was game breaking and needed to be fixed ASAP. Other "minor" bugs have been reported and will be fixed in future patches. 

Thanks for all the feedback. Errors and bugs will get fixed as quickly as possible. 

[h1]Edit: Version 1.4.2 is now live.[/h1] This includes a fix that could cause the game to crash when a player's last warehouse is destroyed.

[h1]Edit: Version 1.4.3 is now live.[/h1] This includes a fix that was preventing players from joining multiplayer games. 

[h1]Edit: Version 1.4.4 is now live.[/h1] This includes a fix that was preventing watchtowers from targeting enemy balloons in multiplayer games. Also a fix for building flags showing the wrong color in multiplayer.

notes.title: FTF Version 1.4
notes.content:
[h1]New Maps[/h1]
With the new build comes a new multiplayer map plus more single player combat maps bringing the total to 5. 

The new multiplayer map is a desert oasis with palm trees and cactus. The level is also playable as a single player.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10000190/acfea8af74dd2e1e8b7d781f6c258ac127137b9d.png[/img]

The additional single player maps range from easy to finish in the “Skirmish” map to much longer experiences in “Desert Oasis” and “Islands in the Sky.” 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10000190/7cf70fd3fcf7eabbabf8be9460a0160715540365.png[/img]

[h1]Leaving Early Access[/h1]
No game is ever finished or ever perfect and Fracture the Flag certainly falls into that category, but the time for FTF to leave the nest has come. 

FTF has come a long way from its first release. The number of bugs, improvements and added features is too hard to count. As a solo developer I have learned so much during the development and release of FTF - I’m more than excited to apply everything that I’ve learned to my next game. Support for the game will continue but will be mostly focused on addressing bugs and not content addition.  

Fracture the Flag will likely leave Early Access in the next few days - any unforeseen bugs, issues or acts of God aside.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10000190/326511f19633dbd0863d69698c890610102df50b.gif[/img]

[h1]Changes & Improvements[/h1]
Version 1.4 while adding substantial content also addressed some bugs and improved some aspects of the game.
[list]
[*]AI attack delay timer no longer starts when the map is loaded, but waits until the player starts.
[*]Watchtower arrow’s damage was substantially reduced.
[*]Matchmaking should be more reliable - hopefully no more joining but being on the wrong map.
[*]Many of the particle effects will now be culled at distance - small performance boost.
[*]Single Player best times should now display properly for all challenges.
[*]The player ranking calculation has been retooled and simplified - the leader board was also reset.
[*]AI bomber behavior has been changed to send groups of bombers rather than individuals on higher difficulty settings.
[*]New combat achievements have been added including a “hard mode” achievement.
[*]Probably a few other bits as well...
[/list]

A few more changes have been made to FTF for version 1.3.1.

notes.title: FTF Version 1.3
notes.content:
[h1]New Features[/h1]
With the new version comes two notable new features! Both should add gameplay and make FTF feel more complete. 

Bomb Balloons are created at the bomb depot and drop 3 powerful bombs on a distant target. They are designed to be single use and will crash after dropping their bombs. 

Defensive watchtowers fire flaming arrows at enemy workers, swordsman, bombers and siege weapons. Watchtowers are also capable of shooting down bomb balloons.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10000190/3775cf90c14f8ca087d3199e15cb55f9f6883622.png[/img]

A short teaser of the new features.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D-2NoMt4B4c
[h1]Other Changes[/h1]
A few other changes have been made to FTF. 
[list]
[*]A population cap of 50 workers has been put in place
[*]Lumber production has been increased
[*]Siege weapon menu has been removed - it was pretty useless
[*]When bombers die they now drop their bomb which explodes
[*]Ammo Depots now have a max amount of ammo - reduces resource drain by over filling
[*]The tech tree has been reduced in size and complexity
[*]The single player AI can now send bomb balloons and will have watchtower defenses
[/list]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10000190/f67785ff9565e6adf22fb94b999621acbb848850.png[/img]

[h1]Networking[/h1]
Further changes to the workers and siege weapon ammo scripts have been made to further reduce network traffic. This should help to further stabilize multiplayer connections. 

Bricks (flags and brick walls) remain the last potential reduction in network traffic. However, accuracy with bricks is more important than with other objects in the game. So changes won’t be made unless there is clearly an issue. 

[h1]Polish and Bug Fixes[/h1]
Several small behind the scene changes have been made too. See the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/388900/discussions/4/350533172682523176/] Change Log [/url] for more complete details

[h1]Next Steps[/h1]
The biggest focus will be on creating more maps or levels. This will take the form of more single player combat options as well as a third multiplayer map. Finishing these new levels will be the final steps before FTF moves out of Early Access. The current hope is that FTF will leave Early Access by the end of the year, but it could be as late as February. 

[h1]Price Changing[/h1]
Before FTF leaves Early Access the game will see an increase in price. The final full price is likely to be near 5 USD. So if FTF has been sitting on your wishlist then buy it before the price increases!

notes.title: New Beta Build - Higher FPS
notes.content:
[h1]Better Frame Rate[/h1]
TL;DR New build is up to 60% faster! FInd it on the Beta Branch.

Fracture the Flag’s game engine was just updated to the most current release state. With this new version comes better optimization for multi-core CPUs. Some of the load from the main thread is now (supposedly) off loaded to a second thread. In brief testing a 30% reduction in CPU time per frame was seen simply by upgrading the engine! 

Furthermore, the precomputed lightmaps have been removed from each level. This cuts the build size of FTF nearly in half. This also seems to have the added benefit of of further reducing the CPU time per frame.  You may notice a change in some of the lighting/coloring.

The two changes combined showed almost a 60% reduction in CPU time from the previous build. This build needs some more testing especially on a wide range of hardware.

Please leave feedback in the comments below.

[h1]How to Switch Branches[/h1]
Switching branches is easy!
[list]
[*]Right click “Fracture the Flag” in your steam library
[*]Click properties
[*]Go to the BETAS tab
[*]Select "beta_testers”
[*]Hit ok and run the update (you may need to restart Steam to force the update)
[/list]
To switch back repeat the steps, but choose “none” to opt out of the beta.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10000190/da1072c3c04e26d44978a3fa4d09659f02115fd4.png[/img]

notes.title: October Update
notes.content:
[h1]Single Player Combat[/h1]
The latest build on the main branch now includes basic single player combat. At the moment this is limited to one level, but will likely expand with feedback from players. Feedback on difficulty, fun factor and bugs are always helpful for the further development of FTF.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10000190/1a8c2009bf6da314650fc7a8bd0591d3a236c573.png[/img]

[h1]Network Disconnects[/h1]
This build also includes the ability to self report on multiplayer disconnects. The game will be gathering data on the number of npcs, number of bricks (walls), and the ip address for location purposes.  These three factors are the key suspects in causing the disconnects. 

Development will now shift to solving or reducing the disconnects. This will be done by attempting to reduce the number of messages sent from player to player. Another option is to allow players to connect to more local servers - getting player locations will help to determine if this is a good solution.

Please report multiplayer disconnects on [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/388900/discussions/4/343786746009206756/]this thread[/url] the more info the quicker a solution can be found.

[h1]Update 10/16[/h1]
Changes have been made to the way the workers data is sent between players. This cuts the number of messages sent by each worker by a factor of 50 and seems to reduce the needed bandwidth as well. The hope is this will provide more stability and fewer disconnects.

notes.title: Single Player Combat
notes.content:
Work on the single player combat has been moving along at a slow but steady pace. The basic pieces are in place and are now working well enough that they need more eyes to further refine and balance the game. 

[h1]New Beta Tester Build[/h1]
The latest build of FTF has been pushed up to the  “Beta Testers” branch. No password is needed and can be tested by everyone!

The build includes one single player combat based challenge. More combat levels will follow once the bugs have been fixed. 

The new build will also self report statistics for a multiplayer disconnect. Resolving or reducing the disconnects will be the next goal after the combat bits are dialed, but getting more data on the disconnects is crucial to solving the problem

[h1]How to Switch Branches[/h1]
Switching branches is easy!
[list]
[*]Right click “Fracture the Flag” in your steam library
[*]Click properties
[*]Go to the BETAS tab
[*]Select "beta_testers”
[*]Hit ok and run the update (you may need to restart Steam to force the update)
[/list]
To switch back repeat the steps, but choose “none” to opt out of the beta.

[h1]Why Beta?[/h1]
Many scripts have been adapted from multiplayer to allow both single and multiplayer. This may cause some issues in multiplayer that would be unacceptable for a main branch release. 

[h1]Known Issues[/h1]
There are a few known issues...
[list]
[*]Not all AI siege weapons fire
[*]Menu shows a second level that does not exist (yet)
[*]White capsule in AI base - serves as a spawn point
[*]Best Times not showing correctly in single player menu
[*]No achievement implemented for combat level
[*]Ability to move swordsman and siege weapons broke - this is game breaking but not easily reproducible
[/list]

notes.title: September Update - AI is Coming
notes.content:
Development on Fracture the Flag has slowed as real life gets hectic, but development does continue! 

The current project is adding to the single player challenges with the addition of some basic combat oriented levels. The new levels will continue to be time based - how fast can you take out the AI base. It will not be a full blown single player campaign - as a solo dev it’s just not possible to pull that off so I won’t promise what I can’t deliver. 

AI bases will have a functional economy to support their attacks on the player’s base. If there’s no ammo then the siege weapons will fall silent. If build points run dry the AI can’t recruit more workers or swordsman… 

The AI will not be capable of adding new building or siege weapons. The AI base is largely static, once a player destroys a building, siege weapon, or flag it’s gone. However, workers and swordsman will be replaced.

The AI is capable of both offense and defense. Sending groups of swordsman to attack buildings and delivering bombs to the base of flags and other buildings. Defensively swordsman will patrol or stand and guard. Siege weapons will also fire if you get too close.

There are lots of little bugs and plenty of balancing to work on. So no promises on a release date. The first release will likely be on the beta channel as many scripts have been adapted to allow the AI which will then need testing to ensure multiplayer didn’t break…

[h1]What’s Next?[/h1]
After the combat AI is released and acceptably bug free my focus will shift to the network disconnect issue. While some disconnects may be the result of poor internet connections or lag to the servers (US based) many or even most are caused by a spike in network traffic which causes loss of information and the servers think there is a disconnect… The networking is done by a third party (Photon). The likely solution is to change how much information is sent. The biggest data hogs are the workers and potentially the brick walls. 

After that… On to the stretch goals. 

And then a full Steam Release. Goodbye Early Access.

notes.title: New Camera - Smoother and Better Rotation
notes.content:
You asked for better camera motion. So here you go! 

With some key insights from a couple players the rotation mechanics of the camera have been altered. The camera no longer rotates around its own axis. If a unit or building is selected the camera will rotate around the selected object. If no unit is selected the camera will rotate around the object in the center of the screen.

Feedback also suggested that the camera motion did not feel smooth. So! Camera motion now includes inertia which significantly smooths out the motion and rotation. Feels buttery smooth. 

[h1]Couple other bits to note[/h1]

Vertical rotation can be enabled in the settings menu, but needs refinement with the new rotation mechanic - use with caution.

The issue where the camera bottoms out on the terrain or other obstacle and does a herky-jerky dance upwards still exists - this issue is most pronounced when using the mouse scroll wheel. 

[h1]Feedback[/h1]
As always your feedback is needed and is crucial to the development of FTF. So let’s hear it! How does the new system feel?

notes.title: New worker System & Optimization - Version 1.1.0
notes.content:
[h1]New Worker System[/h1]
Version 1.1.0 brings the new worker system and worker menu. This new system was the result of player feedback and the desire to minimize micro management. 

The new system is request based. Players can now place requests for workers at individual buildings or via the new worker menu. When workers are available they will fill the requests in the order that they were placed. There is a basic 3-tier priority system to let players fine tune the assignment of workers - highest priority requests are filled first. It’s also worth noting that recruits such as swordsman now also work on the request system - recruits are given further priority over other jobs. 

This also means that if workers are killed a request for a new worker will be placed. So keeping your economy balanced is quicker and easier. This also goes for workers reloading siege weapons - each siege weapon can have up to 5 workers - with the intention of effectively “shortening” supply lines.

At this time there are no known major bugs with the worker system - which means you guys will probably have plenty of feedback shortly… As always bug will be fixed and addressed as soon as possible.

[h1]New Worker Menu[/h1]
As the worker menu serves now as more of a management tool it can be open while other menus such as the build menu are also open. The worker menu can be moved by dragging the top panel. The worker menu can be toggled off by the button under the minimap as before as well as using the escape key (twice).

I would love to hear feedback on this style of menu and if the build menu should follow a similar style 

[h1]Fixes and Optimizations[/h1]
[list]
[*]Significant optimizations to the workers have been made. Testing shows the frame rate to be stable with 200+ workers and two players. See the change log for more details.
[*]Mini map optimization - should have no noticeable visual effect but some users may notice a FPS improvement.
[*]Issue where some players were stuck on the starting menu for multiplayer games has hopefully be resolved or reduced in frequency.
[*]By player request: Catapult range was reduced (by 20%) 
[/list]

notes.title: Download Getting Stuck?
notes.content:
If you are having trouble downloading FTF or other games you aren't alone!

It would appear that Steam is having some difficulty mainly with European servers/regions. If you have a download that is getting stuck an easy solution is to switch servers.

[h1]To Switch Servers[/h1]
[list]
[*]Under the Steam menu on the top left of the Steam Client click on "Settings"
[*]Select the "Downloads" tab
[*]Under "Download Region" select a different region - Canada has been working for many.
[/list]

For more on the problem you can see this [url=http://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/357288572114759931/?tscn=1465405358 ]Steam Community thread[/url].

As a game developer all I can do is point you to a temporary solution, but I do want to know if you are having trouble downloading the game.

notes.title: FTF Release Date & Stretch Goals
notes.content:
[b]Fracture the Flag will be released on June 9th! [/b]

Fracture the Flag will go on sale for 2.99 USD. Which is lower than previously announced. Why? Simply put the goal of FTF was not to make money but rather to publish a game and build a small community. I have learned so much and greatly enjoyed the experience of creating FTF, but it's getting close to time to release this fledgling game into the wild… 

As an Early Access title FTF is “complete.” That means it is fully playable, but has some bugs plus with any game there are more features that can be added. The intention is that FTF will move from Early Access to a full release over the summer and fall of 2016. 

After nearly two years of development it’s time see how the wider Steam community reacts to FTF. So rather than deliver a roadmap of promised features FTF’s continued develop will be based on stretch goals. 

[h1]Stretch Goals - Based on Sales[/h1]
[list]
[*]1000 - Release third map set in a seismically active region
[*]1500 - Defensive watchtowers added. 
[*]2500 - Macemen and Spearman
[*]5000 - Additional Map added with design based on community input
[*]7500 - Air base with 2 units added
[*]10000 - Additional Map added with design based on community input
[*]20000 - Naval units added with additional “water based map”
[/list]

Got ideas for stretch goals? Love to hear them!

notes.title: April Update: Alpha V 0.6 Build Notes
notes.content:
After the original alpha testing there was plenty to update. Bugs were fixed, updates were made and some polish was added. The intention of the Alpha V 0.6  build is that FTF is now “feature complete” in terms of an Early Access release with the expectation that there are still bugs to squash and polish to be added. See the list below for some of the changes that have been made.

A second round of testing (with some new testers) will be happening.

[h1]Features Added[/h1]
[list]
[*]The [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=619143881]“Construction Yard”[/url] has been added and is now the source of siege weapons
[*]Physics based walls are back!
[*]A tech tree has replaced the upgrade menu. Each new tech costs more than the previous tech.
[*]A [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=611959316]basic melee unit (swordsman)[/url] has been added with guard, attack and patrol behaviors
[*][url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=655686959]Steam Leaderboards[/url] added for “ELO”, players beaten, games started and completion times of single player challenges
[*]Single player challenges (resource based) have been added
[*]Flags added to buildings to help identify ownership
[*]Keys can now be re-mapped via the settings menu
[*]Settings menu now includes support for multiple monitors - change requires a restart of the game
[/list]

[h1]Updates[/h1]
[list]
[*]Damage scripts (bombs and siege weapons) have been greatly improved
[*]Tweaks to colors and image effects
[*]Axes and picks have been added to workers to correspond to their current job
[*]Physics material added to bricks along with other physics balancing with siege weapons
[*]The HUD and all UI should now scale better for both 720p and 1080p displays
[*]Build size down to 200 MB from 300 MB
[/list]

notes.title: FTF Improvements
notes.content:
Fracture the Flag’s first round of testing ended with many great suggestions and plenty of bugs to fix (that was the whole point). All of the major or game breaking bugs have been fixed.

Based on testers suggestions work on several improvements and additions to FTF have been happening over the past several weeks including:

[h1]Completed:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Basic melee ground units (Swordsman) have been added and are recruited from a new building ([url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=606440728]Barracks[/url]). More types of melee units are planned.
[*]Archers have been fixed and will return to FTF.
[*] [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=621304665]Physics based brick walls[/url] will return!!! There are still questions about their performance, but it’s looking hopeful and will need wider testing.
[/list]
[h1]Still in progress:[/h1]
[list]
[*]The “upgrade system” has been replaced with a more [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=633398299] traditional style tech tree[/url]. Cost of upgrades are no longer fixed but will be determined by the total number of upgrades already purchased. So choosing upgrades is a matter of strategy.
[*]A new building, the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=619143881] construction yard, [/url] will be added that will build siege weapons. The building will require workers with the production time depending on the number of workers assigned. Siege weapon movement will also be reworked to be less janky. 
[*]Single player levels. Basic “resource challenges” have been added, but need further work. Other single player modes including combat modes are planned. 
[/list]
[h1]Second Round of Testing[/h1]
Once the “still in progress” improvements have been finished and have passed in house testing there will a second round of testing. Hopefully this second round will occur in the next 2-3 weeks. It likely that a few more testers will be needed...
